newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lehman sees Fed on hold despite Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees Fed on hold despite Greenspan comments.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said on Friday it expects the U.S. Federal Reserve to hold short-term interest rates steady this year despite Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's hawkish comments earlier this week.
"We expect to see the Fed funds rate at 5.25 percent at year-end, exactly where it is today," Lehman Brothers' chief U.S. economist Stephen Slifer told Reuters in Hong Kong.
During his appearance before the U.S. Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday, Greenspan hinted that a pre-emptive tightening may be warranted should the economy continue to show strong growth.
He voiced concern about soaring stock prices and warned of rising wage and inflation pressures.
Slifer said Greenspan was just doing what a Fed chairman is supposed to do -- warning against incipient inflation before price pressures are evident.
But he said the market should focus on the chairman's parting remarks to the Senate in which he said U.S. economic prospects are quite favourable.
Several factors are combining to create a steady growth, low inflation environment in the United States, Slifer said.

These include prudent fiscal policies that have slashed the budget deficit, a rising savings rate as American "baby boomers" age, and modest labour market pressures as productivity gains moderate real wage increases and global competition keeps workers' compensation demands in check.
Slifer expects U.S. gross domestic product to grow 2.0-2.5 percent in 1997 and inflation to moderate to 2.4 percent.
